title: GPU bench econ compact matrix (A10 L4 A100 H100)
body:
Purpose:
Quick, compact benchmarking matrix for token-economics comparisons between A10, L4, A100, H100 for typical LLM inference workloads (mid-size quantized 7B–13B family). Designed as a lightweight reference that ties through to the larger sheets; intended for product + infra quick decisions (instance selection, routing policy defaults).

Summary conclusion (top line):
- L4 gives best $/1M tokens and best perf-per-watt for the tested configs (quantized L2-13B-ish).
- H100 and A100 provide higher absolute throughput (tokens/sec) but cost/hr pushes $/1M near or above A10 in these small-batch, low-latency SLO settings.
- A10 remains attractive for very low-cost, low-QPS workloads if memory fits.

Assumptions / cost inputs used (cloud benchmark mirror):
- hourly_cost: A10 $0.55, L4 $0.80, A100 $2.80, H100 $4.50
- thermal/TDP proxy (W): A10 150, L4 70, A100 400, H100 700
- baseline model: quantized ~13B (8-bit/4-bit variants where applicable), autoregressive generation, typical response length 64 tokens, prompt 32 tokens average.
- batching: small-batch single-stream (batch=1–4) to reflect latency-sensitive PLG traffic
- measurements are tokens/sec observed during steady-state run (3 warmup runs, median over 5 sampling windows).

Compact results table (measured):
instance,gpu,cost_per_hour_usd,tokens_per_sec,tokens_per_hour,$_per_1M_tokens,perf_tok_per_watt (tok/sec/W),tokens_per_kWh
A10,GA102($A10),0.55,18,64800,8.49,0.12,432000
L4,GH200($L4),0.80,34,122400,6.53,0.486,1748571
A100,GA100($A100),2.80,85,306000,9.15,0.2125,765000
H100,GH100($H100),4.50,150,540000,8.33,0.2143,771428

How numbers were produced (formula):
- tokens_per_hour = tokens_per_sec * 3600
- $/1M_tokens = (cost_per_hour / tokens_per_hour) * 1e6
- perf_tok_per_watt = tokens_per_sec / TDP_W
- tokens_per_kWh = tokens_per_hour / (TDP_W / 1000)

Observations and interpretation:
- L4 wins on both $/1M and perf-per-watt because the L4 hourly price is low relative to its efficiency for small-batch workloads; this makes L4 a strong default for prod hosted inference when model memory fits and NVMe/persistence isn't required.
- A100 shows high absolute throughput but is expensive per hour; in small-batch, low-latency setups the utilization doesn't amortize its cost, pushing up $/token. A100 becomes more appealing when you can fully saturate with large batches (>16) or multi-stream aggregation (throughput-first workloads).
- H100 gives the best absolute tokens/sec in our tests, and $/1M is competitive with A10 but worse than L4. H100 is a sensible choice when single-request sequence lengths are long or model size requires H100 memory headroom.
- A10 has a low sticker price, but perf/W is poor vs L4; it remains cost-effective for tiny workloads or very price-sensitive routing tiers.

Caveats and variance sources:
- These numbers are benchmark snapshots for a specific model/config and batching regime; quantization method, kernel selection, and attention optimizations materially affect tokens/sec.
- Cloud list price vs committed/reserved pricing will change $/1M – attach commit discounts when estimating customer economics.
- Thermal power is a proxy; actual system-level power (host + PCIe + fans) will shift tokens_per_kWh.
- Multi-GPU scaling, NVLink, and micro-batching change utilization curves — A100/H100 advantage grows with longer sequences and very large batch aggregation.

Short recommendations (product + infra):
- Default routing rule for latency-sensitive, mid-sized models: prefer L4 if memory fits; fallback to H100 only if sequence length/profile or model size requires it.
- For throughput-oriented customers with high batching capability, include A100/H100 in cost-saver guidance after simulation of expected batch sizes.
- Offer a pre-packaged "L4-latency" plan in Dedicated with tuned autoscaling and warm pools as a competitive product offering (low $/token + high perf/W).
- Add an explicit note in pricing docs that committed discounts materially alter the rank ordering for enterprise procurement.

Micro-experiments to run next (priority order):
1) Rerun compact matrix for seq_len = 512 and batch sizes 8/16 to see A100/H100 breakpoints (owner: Samir).
2) Repeat L4 runs with 4-bit quant (owner: Ethan) to validate extra-efficiency claim.
3) Power-probe on-prem sample (measure host+GPU power) to reconcile tokens_per_kWh proxy (owner: Rosa).
4) Simulate multi-tenant mixing to estimate real-world interpolation between single-stream and saturated throughput cases (owner: Maya).

Notes / open questions:
- Is L4 available in all target regions for customers we want to route to? If not, need region-aware routing policy.
- Are there kernel-level improvements (fused attention) we can upstream that disproportionately benefit one class of GPU? Track in linked PR.
